kg_child_context_reason: The fragments instantiate sd_crc_7 and the BITVAL wiring is potentially ambiguous because both CRC_IN and CRC_OUT appear in the generated logic; child interface/code context can confirm the exact port names, directions, and intended serial CRC bit input wiring.
code_gap_notes: The final merge must preserve the exact split input/output interface and output reg ownership, including ACK_OUT/REQ_OUT/status/CMD line control.

CRC wiring is ambiguous in the fragments: sd_crc_7 BITVAL is connected to CRC_IN[6] while FSM_OUT also drives CRC_OUT as a serial bit signal, so the merge needs authoritative CRC submodule/interface context.
Reset behavior differs by block: synchronizers use asynchronous reset while the command decoder, FSM state update, and FSM_OUT use clocked reset behavior; merge must not homogenize these incorrectly.
Handshake semantics for REQ_IN/ACK_OUT and REQ_OUT/ACK_IN must be preserved so SETTING_IN/CMD_IN stability and completion notification are correct.

FSM_OUT contains most output ownership and status/st_dat_t behavior, including CRC validation and command response buffering, so per-state details are needed to avoid incorrect signal defaults or duplicate drivers.
